The structure of Mg3Fe2Sb crystallizes in the trigonal space group P3 (No. 1), with a unit cell containing six atoms and four independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Fe and Sb centers each surrounded by nine neighbors, while Mg centers have twelve neighbors in a close-packed-like local arrangement; the neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component. Validated polyhedron-sharing analysis indicates corner- and edge-sharing between Fe and Sb 9-vertex polyhedra, and corner-, edge-, and face-sharing between Mg 12-vertex and Fe or Sb polyhedra.
